nodes.label: 3D Swing Visualization
nodes.rationale: Drawing the target line from the address reference frame makes path and face angle visually obvious instead of only numeric.

nodes.label: Address Calibration
nodes.rationale: The club is grounded during the stillness period, giving a known clubhead height of 0 to sanity check plus a square to target reference frame every later face angle and path number is measured against.

nodes.label: Ball Flight Estimate
nodes.rationale: Not aiming for launch monitor accuracy. Without real spin data the face to path difference stands in as a spin axis proxy for curve direction and amount.

nodes.label: BMI270 Sensor Setup
nodes.rationale: Accel +/-16g and gyro +/-2000 dps chosen because both have headroom for high school swing speeds. No magnetometer, so absolute heading is unobservable by design.

nodes.label: Canned Swing Fixtures
nodes.rationale: Good swing, slice tendency, hook tendency, and waggle then swing, so detection and stats both get exercised on known inputs.

nodes.label: Face to Path Difference
nodes.rationale: Face to path, not face to target, is what drives hook and slice, so it is the number reported and the proxy the flight model curves on.

nodes.label: Forward Kinematics Clubhead Position
nodes.rationale: Known club length plus a fixed IMU offset from the grip, rotated by the current orientation quaternion.

nodes.label: Conventional Commit Discipline
nodes.rationale: Small frequent commits after every fix, feat, or chore rather than one giant dump at the end.

nodes.label: Mock IMU Stream Generator
nodes.rationale: No hardware exists yet, so the entire pipeline is developed and tested against canned swings played back at a realistic rate.

nodes.label: Projectile Model with Drag
nodes.rationale: Drag coefficient is hardcoded rather than configurable, since the estimate does not need that level of tuning.

nodes.label: Smash Factor Constant
nodes.rationale: Published typical values per club type, roughly 1.33-1.38 for mid irons and lower for wedges.

nodes.label: Swing Start Detection
nodes.rationale: The record tap happens before the golfer settles into address, so t=0 walks back to the last true stillness point rather than using the tap.

nodes.label: Swing Stats Set
nodes.rationale: Tempo, phase durations, peak angular velocity, clubhead speed at impact, swing plane, attack angle, face angle, path, and face to path.

nodes.label: One Handed Phone UI
nodes.rationale: Used one handed on a driving range or practice green, so a club picker and a big record button dominate and the post swing readout is a single glance.

nodes.label: Waggle Rejection
nodes.rationale: A waggle spikes then returns to baseline and tends to reverse rotational direction. A real takeaway holds above threshold for 100-150ms and stays roughly monotonic in one direction.

nodes.label: Plain Comment and Copy Style Rule
nodes.norm_label: plain comment and copy style rule
nodes.rationale: Short plain comments only where code is not self explanatory, no em dashes anywhere in code, comments, or UI text.

nodes.label: Zero Velocity Updates
nodes.rationale: Address and the top of the backswing are both near zero angular velocity moments, so they anchor orientation error before it builds across the swing.

nodes.label: BMI270 Range Constants
nodes.rationale: 16g and 2000 dps at 400 Hz is about 5.6 kB/s packed as int16. The canned swings peak near 1880 dps and 16g so they deliberately exercise the top of both ranges.

nodes.label: Grip Hand Speed Test
nodes.rationale: Checks recovered hand speed against the synthesizer's known hand motion, the same round trip idea applied to one quantity.

nodes.label: ImuSource
nodes.rationale: Delivers samples in batches because that is how BLE notifications arrive, so the mock and a real sensor have identical shape.

nodes.label: Stick Pipeline Architecture
nodes.rationale: The UI knows about SwingAnalysis and nothing else, the pipeline knows about ImuSource and nothing else. That two sided ignorance is what keeps the sensor swappable.

nodes.label: Pipeline Round Trip Test
nodes.rationale: The synthesizer knows exactly what face angle, path, and speed it produced, so the pipeline has to give those back from nothing but noisy, biased, quantized samples. Recovery inside a degree is the accelerometer bias floor rather than the maths.

nodes.label: Locked Mobile Viewport
nodes.rationale: maximum-scale=1, user-scalable=no and viewport-fit=cover plus mobile-web-app-capable stop pinch zoom and letterboxing during one handed use on a phone at the range.

nodes.label: Driver Out of Scope
nodes.rationale: The driver is the one club that gets teed up, so the grounded club address height calibration would not hold for it. Every other club gets swept off the ground.

nodes.label: IMU Source Interface Boundary
nodes.rationale: Isolating the input layer behind one interface lets a real BLE data source be swapped in later without touching anything downstream.

nodes.label: No Double Integration for Position
nodes.rationale: Double integrating the accelerometer drifts badly over a swing length window, so position becomes a geometry problem via forward kinematics instead of an integration problem.

nodes.label: Phone Browser Performance Constraint
nodes.rationale: Target is iOS Safari on a phone at a driving range, not a dev machine, so math and rendering stay lightweight and unnecessary re-renders are avoided.

nodes.label: Accelerometer Bias Accuracy Floor
nodes.rationale: A still sensor gives one vector, and a tilted sensor is indistinguishable from a sideways biased one. The error is absorbed into the address frame as a tilt of about a degree and carries into every angle measured against it. Only the along gravity component is recoverable. Calibrating the accelerometer is what buys accuracy here, not anything in this repo.

nodes.label: Arm Length Position Constraint
nodes.rationale: Position is still two integrations and still drifts, so direction comes from the integral and distance comes from the arms, a fixed length that cannot drift. That removes the radial error that would visibly stretch and squash the golfer's arms. The residual slides the hands along their own arc and only the replay depends on it.

nodes.label: BLE Swap Point
nodes.rationale: Implementing ImuSource and handing it to SwingDetector in place of MockImuSource is the only change a real sensor requires.

nodes.label: Gyro Bias Estimation
nodes.rationale: A couple of degrees per second left in place integrates into several degrees across a swing, larger than the face angles being reported. It is estimated from the still window before takeaway, which is why that window leaves a guard band ahead of t=0 and filters to genuinely quiet samples.

nodes.label: Hand Speed from the Accelerometer
nodes.rationale: The accelerometer sits at the grip so it sees the grip's own acceleration. Velocity is one integration, not two, and it starts from a boundary condition known for free: the club is still at address. Over the second to impact that holds up.

nodes.label: No Driver Support
nodes.rationale: The address calibration assumes a grounded club and the driver is the one club that gets teed up.

nodes.label: Physically Consistent Mock
nodes.rationale: Acceleration is derived from the same motion that generates the gyro trace. The synthesizer models the hands with its own constants that the analysis never sees, so the pipeline is not graded against its own assumptions. Noise, per axis bias, and quantization are all modelled.

nodes.label: Two Segment Club Model
nodes.rationale: A hub the arms pivot about plus the shaft. Pinning the grip at a point costs about twenty percent of clubhead speed since much of it comes from the hands travelling. It is also a representability question: a 7 iron at 80 mph off a fixed grip needs over 2300 dps at the sensor, past what a BMI270 can report at all.

nodes.label: Two Stage Waggle Rejection
nodes.rationale: A cheap check at 120ms commits to capturing and keeps t=0 accurate. A second check at the end discards anything that got that far and never produced contact, catching a waggle big and slow enough to survive the first pass. Buffering is cheap, so a wrong provisional capture costs nothing.

nodes.label: Yaw Unobservability
nodes.rationale: No magnetometer pins absolute heading, but every reported angle is relative to the address frame and a swing lasts about a second, so drift does not matter. It would matter over minutes, which is why t=0 anchors to the last stillness rather than the record tap.
